sections.title: Overview
sections.body: An agent execution is not a single LLM request. It can contain a hierarchy of decisions, subagents, tool invocations, approval pauses, retries and external transactions.

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments. It can contain a hierarchy of decisions, subagents, tool invocations, approval pauses, retries and external transactions.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

Useful telemetry includes agent and model versions, tool names, sanitized operation identifiers, duration, retries, token usage, decision categories, approval status and verified outcomes.

Do not rely on collecting private model reasoning, full prompts or confidential records to make the system observable.

sections.title: 23.4 OpenTelemetry implementation
sections.body:
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode

tracer = trace.get_tracer(
    "enterprise.agents"
)

def traced_tool_call(
    tool_name,
    execute
):

    with tracer.start_as_current_span(
        "agent.tool.execute"
    ) as span:

        span.set_attribute(
            "agent.tool.name",
            tool_name
        )

        try:

            result = execute()

            span.set_attribute(
                "agent.tool.outcome",
                "returned"
            )

            return result

        except Exception as exc:

            span.set_attribute(
                "error.type",
                type(exc).__name__
            )

            span.set_status(
                Status(StatusCode.ERROR)
            )

            raise
```

Configure the tracer provider, exporter and secure collector separately.

The status `returned` deliberately does not mean that the requested business operation succeeded. That must be verified independently.

sections.title: 23.6 Incident example — All tools return HTTP 200, but task success drops
sections.body:
Possible explanations include tool responses containing business-level errors, incorrect tool selection, missing required milestones, stale data, false completion and output verification regressions.

A health dashboard based only on HTTP status codes cannot diagnose these failures.

Monitor task outcomes separately from transport-level availability.
